recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-26435 unless Patient Care later changes the intended scope of AdverseEvent.resultingEffect.
issue_request: FHIR-26435 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care request to revise AdverseEvent.resultingCondition because the R4 definition limited the element to reactions after exposure to substances, while the condition can result from any adverse event such as a broken leg after a fall.
initial_application: Commit 12d222c23df9fcab9742ec7e7bf1981d84539119 applied J#26435 in the AdverseEvent source spreadsheet by replacing the exposure-only reaction wording with an adverse-event-based definition and adding the broken-leg/fall example. Later source rework carried that definition into structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml.
additional_context: The current build-scoped source uses AdverseEvent.resultingEffect rather than the R4 name. FHIR-34316 renamed resultingCondition to resultingEffect and added Observation as a target, while FHIR-48833 later changed the element to CodeableReference; both retained the FHIR-26435 definition. source/fhir.ini keeps AdverseEvent active and maps AdverseEvent.resultingCondition to AdverseEvent.resultingEffect for R4-R6 change tracking.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. The current definition already describes the resulting condition as occurring from the adverse event, includes both substance-exposure and fall examples, and is attached to the current renamed element.

related_jiras.note: Renamed AdverseEvent.resultingCondition to AdverseEvent.resultingEffect and added Observation while preserving the FHIR-26435 definition.
Changed AdverseEvent.resultingEffect to CodeableReference and retained the FHIR-26435 wording.
